clue.text: As — a heavenly body

parts.note: give SA a turn and it becomes the clue's word As

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry pairing a short word with a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, split into SA and TURN, is an instruction that produces the clue word. SA turned round gives AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth planet from the Sun is a celestial object, which is what a heavenly body is.

clue.text: With five arms a brilliant swimmer

definitions.text: With five arms a brilliant swimmer

parts.note: a star is something brilliant, a shining light
a fish is a creature that swims

explanation.surface: A five-limbed creature that swims superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-armed sea creature, an echinoderm, which the clue describes as a shining swimmer.

clue.text: She changes her habitat

indicators.note: the word habitat is altered, its letters rearranged into a woman's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges HABITAT into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so a she.

clue.text: Snobby for snubby

parts.note: a snub nose turns up, and a snob turns up their nose

explanation.walkthrough: A turned-up nose is snub; turning up one's nose is snobbish, so one word for 'turned up' fits both.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a nose, turned up at the tip, which suggests disdain.

clue.text: He may have to look for a job

definitions.text: He may have to look for a job

parts.words: He may have to look for a job
parts.note: reads as an unemployed man hunting for work, but means a man whose work is simply looking on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for a job' suggests job-hunting; here looking is the job itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher's employment consists of looking, so he looks for a living.

clue.text: It does not have to go with trading stamps

definitions.text: It does not have to go with trading stamps

parts.words: It does not have to go with trading stamps
parts.note: trading stamps were retail reward tokens; here it means postage stamps on commercial mail

explanation.walkthrough: Trading stamps were tokens given with purchases; the clue means correspondence about trade, which needs postage stamps, not trading ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal correspondence concerning trade or commerce.

clue.text: Here, of course, poems may be composed

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the word poems is rearranged into a place name

explanation.surface: A place where verse may naturally be written.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'may be composed' works on POEMS. 'Of course' means a racecourse: Epsom Downs in Surrey hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey town famous for its racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Where two gents with money produce a drug on the market

parts.note: Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona names the Italian city
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Two men with cash supplying narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The Two Gentlemen of Verona is Shakespeare's play. Veronal was a trade name for barbital, a sleeping drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietary barbiturate sleeping powder sold under a brand name.

clue.text: Something for a Baconian to get his teeth into?

definitions.text: Something for a Baconian to get his teeth into?

parts.words: Something for a Baconian to get his teeth into?
parts.note: a Baconian is a follower of Francis Bacon; here a bacon-lover chewing a slice

explanation.walkthrough: Baconians claim Francis Bacon wrote Shakespeare; read literally, a Baconian eats bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of bacon to eat.

clue.text: The best in a display of jumpers

definitions.text: The best in a display of jumpers

parts.words: The best in a display of jumpers
parts.note: jumpers sounds like knitwear, but means show-jumping horses

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' suggests sweaters (British for pullovers); the display is a show-jumping event and the best is the year's champion horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A title awarded to the champion show-jumping mount of a season.

clue.text: It came daily to the mariner's hollo

definitions.text: It came daily to the mariner's hollo

parts.words: It came daily to the mariner's hollo
parts.note: quotes Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, where a great seabird came every day to the sailor's call

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem says the bird 'every day, for food or play, came to the mariner's hollo'; hollo is an old word for a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabird in Coleridge's Rime answered the sailors' calls each day before being shot.

clue.text: Being out of them might induce bad feeling:

definitions.text: Being out of them might induce bad feeling

parts.words: Being out of them might induce bad feeling
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'out of ...', meaning unwell or grumpy, as if being out of stock of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' reads as having run short of something; the idiom 'out of sorts' means feeling off-colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinds or varieties; to be lacking them, in the idiom, is to feel unwell or irritable.

clue.text: Six-footers, all at sea

parts.note: reads as tall men who are confused, but describes nautical units of six feet used to measure depth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footers' suggests tall people and 'all at sea' bewilderment; both are literal here, a unit of six feet used at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of depth, each six feet long, used for sounding water by sailors.

clue.text: He's evidently someone's choice

parts.note: describes a person put forward or named by someone, so plainly picked

explanation.definitionFit: A person proposed for office or an award has been named, that is chosen, by another.

clue.text: The remaining supporters ?

definitions.meaning: stopping on, as in the verb sense of staying put; a guest's continued presence
corsets stiffened to hold the body up, or ropes bracing a mast

explanation.surface: A question about the last of a group of fans still left.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining in a place is staying; and the plural also names old-fashioned corsets and a ship's bracing ropes that hold things up.

clue.text: The race problem can be surmounted

definitions.text: The race problem can be surmounted

parts.words: The race problem can be surmounted
parts.note: sounds like a social issue, but describes a hurdle in a race of barriers that runners climb over

explanation.walkthrough: 'The race problem' suggests racial politics; the race is an athletic one with things to climb over.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier or hurdle is something in the way that can be got over.

clue.text: Get a communist back ' after conviction

indicators.note: says the reversed piece comes after the first piece

parts.note: to attain is to get or achieve

indicators.note: the word for a communist is read backwards

parts.note: red is a familiar term for a communist

explanation.surface: Bringing a party member home once the guilty verdict is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is a common nickname for a communist. Attainder was the old English legal penalty: a person sentenced for treason or felony lost their property and civil rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, the forfeiture of rights that followed a sentence for treason, effectively the condemnation itself.

clue.text: William's ancestry ?

parts.note: a Williams is a variety of pear, so its family tree is the fruit tree it grows on

explanation.walkthrough: Williams is a pear variety; its 'family tree' is the tree it grows on.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit tree that bears pears, the Williams variety's origin.

clue.text: One trial is sufficient for him

indicators.note: the two words supply enough letters to make the person once rearranged, which is the old-style anagram signal here

explanation.surface: A man so able that a single attempt is all he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One trial is sufficient' means the letters of ONE TRIAL are all that is needed to build him once they are rearranged; there is no other anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Him here stands for a person from the East, a native of Asia.

clue.text: The Sound of Music-a poem

indicators.note: the answer has the sound of a word for a piece of music

parts.note: a rondo is a musical form with a recurring theme

explanation.surface: A nod to the famous film musical, with verse attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound of Music' is the film title, but here it means a word sounding like a musical piece, RONDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A short French verse form with a refrain and two rhymes.

clue.text: It sounds a workmanlike material

indicators.note: says the answer has the sound of another word, given by the following clue word

parts.note: a workman's implement, a tool, is the workmanlike thing whose name is heard

explanation.walkthrough: The fabric's name is said like TOOL, the workman's implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine net fabric used for veils and ballet skirts is a kind of material.

clue.text: Someone you may be willing to help

definitions.text: Someone you may be willing to help

parts.words: Someone you may be willing to help
parts.note: willing means making a will, so the person helped is left something in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' means writing a will in their favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A beneficiary who inherits under a will.

clue.text: Ants encountered in a German river

indicators.note: the word for encountered sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ems is a river in north-west Germany
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Insects found in a river in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An old dialect word for ants.

clue.text: It's one in the eye for its owner

definitions.text: It's one in the eye for its owner

parts.words: It's one in the eye for its owner
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'one in the eye', a setback, for a single lens worn in one eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'One in the eye' means a snub or defeat; here it is literally a single glass worn in one eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A single eyeglass held in one eye socket.

clue.text: Petty sort of remark ?

parts.note: petty plays on 'pet', a cat, as well as mean-spirited

explanation.walkthrough: Petty means spiteful, and puns on pets: a cat-like remark is a spiteful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful and sly in speech, as feline comments are said to be.

clue.text: The one, under pressure, to cause an outbreak of fire

definitions.text: The one, under pressure, to cause an outbreak of fire

parts.words: The one, under pressure, to cause an outbreak of fire
parts.note: reads as a person who cracks under stress and starts a blaze, but describes the gun lever pressed to fire a shot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' means shooting, not flames, and the pressure is a finger's.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's lever is squeezed to discharge the weapon.

clue.text: It is proverbially foreshadowed

parts.note: points to the proverb 'coming ... cast their shadows before'

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'Coming events cast their shadows before'.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening or occurrence, which the proverb says sends its shadow ahead.

clue.text: He is expected to give correct change

definitions.text: He is expected to give correct change

parts.words: He is expected to give correct change
parts.note: sounds like a shop cashier counting coins, but describes someone who makes corrections to a text

explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct change' suggests money at a till; it means changes that correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrector of texts makes alterations that put errors right.

clue.text: Tale told with a nautical twist?

definitions.text: Tale told with a nautical twist?

parts.words: Tale told with a nautical twist?
parts.note: a story told is a yarn spun; at sea it is also twisted rope-yarn

explanation.walkthrough: To spin a yarn is to tell a tale; sailors' small line made of twisted yarns has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cord of twisted strands used on ships, and literally a story that has been told.

clue.text: Something to go round the walls of a cold-storage chamber?

definitions.text: Something to go round the walls of a cold-storage chamber?

parts.words: Something to go round the walls of a cold-storage chamber?
parts.note: a decorative band round a room's walls whose name is said like the word for chilling to ice

explanation.walkthrough: A decorative band round a wall shares its sound with what a cold store does.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental horizontal band near the top of a wall.
